{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
sales_df = pd.read_csv('data/sales.csv')

# Convert 'revenue' to float
sales_df['revenue'] = pd.to_numeric(sales_df['revenue'], errors='coerce')

# Verify the premises
# 1. Are both email and paid_search present?
channels_present = set(sales_df['channel'].unique())
expected_channels = {'email', 'paid_search'}
channels_match = channels_present == expected_channels

# 2. Is 'converted' binary (0/1)?
converted_is_binary = set(sales_df['converted'].unique()) == {0, 1}

# 3. Conversion rate is proportion of converted out of exposed
# We define exposure as total records per channel

# Compute conversion rates
conversion_rates = sales_df.groupby('channel')['converted'].mean()

# Extract conversion rates for email and paid_search
c_email = conversion_rates['email']
c_paid_search = conversion_rates['paid_search']

# Compute the difference
difference = c_email - c_paid_search

# Print results
print("Channels present:", channels_present)
print("Expected channels:", expected_channels)
print("Channels match?", channels_match)
print("Converted is binary?", converted_is_binary)
print("Conversion rate - email:", c_email)
print("Conversion rate - paid_search:", c_paid_search)
print("Difference (email - paid_search):", difference)"}
